nodes.label: Custom extension runtime
nodes.rationale: Not a full Chrome implementation: WebKitGTK cannot install .crx packages or run Chrome's webRequest/declarativeNetRequest/service-worker model, so background pages are hosted in offscreen windows and only a practical chrome.* subset is supported. Content scripts share Kite's content manager, so they also run in incognito tabs.

nodes.label: kite:// internal pages
nodes.rationale: Internal pages give settings, history, bookmarks, profiles, sync and extensions a UI without a native dialog toolkit dependency; content scripts are blocked on them for safety.

nodes.label: kite.db SQLite store
nodes.rationale: History, bookmarks and pinned links share one SQLite file because queries (omnibox suggestions, start page) span all three; session state lives separately in session.ini at mode 0600.

nodes.label: Omnibox suggestions and completion
nodes.rationale: Local-first: suggestions come from history, bookmarks, pins and open tabs before any network search, so no remote suggest service is contacted.

nodes.label: Named and guest profiles
nodes.rationale: Each named profile gets its own config/data directories for isolated history, bookmarks, settings, extensions and website data; switching writes an active-profile marker and relaunches because WebKit contexts cannot be re-scoped in place. Guest mode is a throwaway directory deleted on exit.

nodes.label: Session restore and recently closed tabs
nodes.norm_label: session restore and recently closed tabs
nodes.rationale: Restore opens the previous pinned tabs first and then an active fresh start page, so restoring never blocks a clean new-tab start; incognito state is never persisted.

nodes.label: settings.ini configuration
nodes.rationale: Plain INI in ~/.config/kite keeps settings human-editable and greppable; it also doubles as storage for permission decisions and per-host zoom, avoiding a second config format.

nodes.label: Split view (two tabs side by side)
nodes.norm_label: split view (two tabs side by side)
nodes.rationale: Toolbar, navigation and find bar follow the focused pane, so one set of chrome serves both panes instead of duplicating controls.

nodes.label: kite://newtab start page
nodes.rationale: Custom quick links are stored separately from pinned tabs because pinned links belong to history/pin storage while start-page links are pure appearance config.

nodes.label: Folder-based sync
nodes.rationale: Sync is a user-chosen folder plus a kite-sync.json file rather than a server, keeping the browser dependency-free; cookies, passwords and extensions intentionally stay local.

nodes.label: Omnibox URL normalization rules
nodes.rationale: localhost/IP -> http, domains -> https, absolute paths -> file://, everything else -> Google search; defaults to https for security while keeping local dev addresses working.

nodes.label: kite_add_browser()
nodes.rationale: Single helper builds any browser executable from src/main.cpp plus KITE_UI_SOURCES, so optimized and debug binaries stay in sync and land in the source dir for direct ./mybrowser runs.

nodes.label: mybrowser-debug executable target
nodes.rationale: Excluded from ALL and built with -g -O0 -UNDEBUG so asserts stay live only on demand.

nodes.label: Kite Browser
nodes.rationale: A lightweight Linux browser built on GTK3 + WebKitGTK rather than Chromium; the WebKit base is what forces the extension and ad-block design limits documented later.

nodes.label: Kite application icon
nodes.rationale: 128x128 scalable icon: a blue vertical gradient rounded square (26px radius) holding a faceted white/light-blue kite diamond with a white tail triangle. Flat, high-contrast, and legible at dock/favicon sizes.

nodes.label: Faceted kite diamond glyph
nodes.rationale: The diamond is split into four shaded quadrants plus a tail, giving the mark depth with only flat fills so it renders identically at small sizes.

nodes.label: BUILD_TESTING test suite
nodes.rationale: One CTest executable per kite_core module (url_utils, settings, history, session, adblock_rules, profile, omnibox, sync) plus a Python filter test when an interpreter exists; only core-linked logic is covered, UI is not.

nodes.label: kite_core static library
nodes.rationale: Testable, UI-independent logic is separated into a static library so unit tests can link it without GTK/WebKit; links only glib, sqlite3 and JavaScriptCore.

nodes.label: Ad blocking (content blockers + in-page YouTube removal)
nodes.norm_label: ad blocking (content blockers + in-page youtube removal)
nodes.rationale: Uses WebKit content blockers instead of Chrome's declarativeNetRequest or webRequest, which WebKitGTK does not provide; YouTube ads are removed in-page because they are first-party.

nodes.label: filters.json generated filters
nodes.rationale: Generated from a domain list by update_filters.py; loaded from the executable's directory or CWD as fallback, so install must ship it next to the binary.

nodes.label: Persistent dark mode with hue preservation
nodes.norm_label: persistent dark mode with hue preservation
nodes.rationale: Recolors page colors preserving hue instead of inverting them, because inversion ruins images and brand colors; a Google Search fallback handles gradient result cards that CSS recoloring misses.
